sections.content:
[BEFORE MIDTERM]
- Curves theory, curvature and torsion, plane curves, fundamental theorem of space curves
Frenet-Serret frame; surface theory: Weingarten map, first and second fundamental forms, curvatures, Gaussian map, ruled surface, minimal surface;
[AFTER MIDTERM]
- Covariant derivatives, Theorema Egregium
- Geodesic curvature, Gauss-Bonnet theorem
nstrinsic geometry: Theorema Egregium, Coddazi-Mainardi equations, parallel transport, geodesics, exponential map, Gauss-Bonnet theorem.
sections.teaching: The explanations are clear and thorough, all concepts are explained very well. Studying under FF, the lectures are very detailed, and the notes are very clear and easy to understand, with many examples to aid comprehension. The class pace is excellent; don't miss the lectures, they will be incredibly beneficial.
sections.grading: I didn't do well on my midterm exam, but the two scoring systems helped me get a pretty good grade in the end. Overall, the scoring system was quite good.
sections.workload: The workload is manageable, with five assignments in total, each consisting of about five questions, plus a midterm and final exam. Overall, it's not too heavy.

sections.content:
Review of calculus & linear algebra; curves; manifolds; Gauss-pontryagin map; tensors; local representations; Lie derivative, covariant derivative (optional).

Mt covers everything up to curves. So you really begin to learn differential geometry for half a semester. Some important concepts (I think they might be important) like curvature, Riemann tensor, covariant derivative, Stokes’s theorem are not taught in-depth but simply mentioned. I reckon that this course better be changed its name to ‘introduction to differential geometry’.
sections.teaching:
Prof. Meng  is good at telling funny stories and not-so-funny ones, with the latter kind being the content covered in this course. There are many signs, jargons and definitions to be remembered, which can always be confusing. But he ‘naturally’ handled them all, hence you can infer from his teaching that he is indeed quite knowledgeable in math. Prof spoke relatively fast, so you have to pay attention to follow his pace.

Despite the grades given, Prof. Meng is actually an interesting person. You will enjoy the lectures if you indeed focus on them.
sections.grading: You can see this semester’s grade distribution from another review.  The grades were not good, for me, I scored 73/80 in mt and 82/100 in final, with mean 55/80 and 60/100 respectively, ended up with a B+. Yeah I have to say my final was like a joke for I conducted many stupid mistakes, but this grade was totally unexpected.
sections.workload: Treat the hw problems carefully, as only by doing them can you further understand the concepts and formulae. If you show sufficient effort in solving the problems in your hw, you will automatically get full marks.

sections.teaching:

and explained later. Try to follow his thinking patterns.

No worry for his English, which is among the best of Math Dept.

sections.content: 佢教既野同佢教另一個PG course differential topology既野根本一樣。佢應該assume左全部人都係讀honor linear algebra 再讀佢果科。
sections.teaching:
佢話作為一個mathematican應該要張d野自己develop出黎而唔係就咁聽人教，所以佢教既content係佢自己develop既，用既notation都係佢自己創既。所以好多時會唔知佢講d咩。如果想理解佢講既野建議睇果本Differential Geometry: Curves - Surfaces - Manifolds, Second Edition
應該同佢用既notation有相似。
sections.grading: 佢話佢既grading比math department既grading好喎，有18% A，但係個course 本身就少人讀，好唔好grade就自己諗啦。
sections.workload: 功課有做就有分，不過佢d hw都係要你proof一d有用既theorem但係佢上堂就唔會教。
